DA hike for central government employees: Can government announce dearness allowance increase on Wednesday?
 By Shaghil Bilali , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 27, 2026, 05:35:17 PM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 DA news: More than 55 lakh central government employees are anticipating a dearness allowance hike announcement soon. The hike is expected to be announced following the cabinet meeting scheduled for October 28, 2026. If approved, the DA rate may increase from 60% to an estimated 63%, resulting in salary increases. Employees are hopeful for the announcement after delayed expectations in previous meetings this month. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online DA news for central government employees With Diwali around the corner, more than 5.5 million central government employees are hoping for an announcement regarding a dearness allowance (DA) hike. The weekly Cabinet meeting is scheduled on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), which raises the expectations that the government may announce the DA hike and bring an end to employees’ long wait.
 Can the central government announce DA hike on Wednesday? 
If the government holds its weekly Cabinet meeting as scheduled on Wednesday (October 28), it may announce the DA hike after the meeting. 
Manjeet Singh Patel, President of the All India New Pension Scheme Employees’ Association, told ET Wealth Online that since it’s a big announcement—also for the government—it can announce it after the scheduled meeting on Wednesday.
Also Read: EPS-95 higher pension: Pensioners’ body appeals to President as retirees struggle to get higher pensio n
Since the beginning of the festive season this year, employees and pensioners have been waiting for the announcement. There were high expectations that the hike would be announced a day after Dussehra on the October 22 Cabinet meeting, but the government didn’t hold its weekly Cabinet meeting last week.
 Long wait but no DA hike announcement 
The DA hike will be calculated from July 2026. So, when the Labour Bureau released the retail index reading for June at July-end, expectations were high that the government would announce it in September ahead of Dussehra. But the government didn’t do so.
Expectations were also high that the DA hike announcement would come after the first weekly Cabinet meeting on October 6, but employees were left disappointed.
Many believed that the government wouldn’t delay it beyond the second weekly Cabinet meeting of the month on October 14. However, the government made the big announcement of the performance-linked bonus for Railway employees but didn’t say anything about the DA hike.
Also Read: No additional EPS contribution by government on higher wage ceiling of Rs 25,000; know what it means for your pension 
On October 16, the government even announced the non-performance-linked bonus (non-PLB) for central non-gazetted government employees but skipped the DA announcement.
With bonuses already declared, employees were expecting that the government would announce the DA hike after the Cabinet meeting on October 21. But they were again left disappointed as the government didn’t hold the weekly meeting.
 DA rate applicability 
Patel says that the DA rate will be applicable for the July-December 2026 period. If the government announces it this month, employees will get arrears for the July-October period along with their salary at the end of November, says Patel. This is because pay is calculated from the 15th of one month to the 15th of the next month.
Also Read: DR hike for pensioners: As government delays release of dearness relief and arrears, Bharat Pensioners' Samaj urges cabinet secretary to intervene 
 What can be the DA hike: 3 or 4 percentage points ? 
For the DA calculation, the average retail inflation of July 2025-June 2026 will be considered. Applying the average inflation to the DA calculation formula, the estimated DA hike can be 3 percentage points. This means that the current DA rate can go up from 60% to 63%.
 How DA impacts the salary of a central government employee 
Employees get the DA based on their basic pay. When the DA increases, their gross salary also increases. Another salary component attached to the DA is the transport allowance (TPTA), which also increases with the DA hike.
Take the example of a Level 8 employee residing in a higher TPTA city, such as New Delhi. Their starting basic salary is Rs 47,600, and the TPTA allowance is Rs 3,200. If the DA rises from 60% to 63%, there will be an increase of approximately Rs 1,428 a month in their DA.
However, their overall transport allowance will also increase from Rs 5,760 to Rs 5,868, a Rs 108 increase. (Join our ETWealth WhatsApp channel for all the latest updates)
